newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton futures close down on consumption data.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton futures close down on consumption data.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures closed weaker on speculative selling sparked by U.S. consumption data and weakness in soybean futures, market sources said.
Trade buying at the low was too light to absorb losses, dealers said.
Benchmark May closed down 0.90 at 73.35 cents per lb, having ranged from 74.20 to 73.10 cents. The rest of the board settled unchanged to 0.79 cent weaker.
Support in May was pegged between 73.00 and 72.50 cents and then at 70.00 cents. The upside target was seen at 75.50.
Volume was estimated at a brisk 25,000 lots compared to Thursday's official 6,906 lots.
The U.S. Census Bureau put February consumption at a seasonally-adjusted annual rate of 10.798 million 480-lb bales, and revised downward the January figure to 10.983 million bales.
Expectations were for 11.0 million bales in February.

National Cotton Council economist Mark Lange said despite the estimate, the U.S. remains on track to consume the 11.0 million bales projected by the U.S. Department of Agriculture in its most recent report.
"We think that for the crop year, 11.0 million bales is still a good number and anticipate mill use next year would climb to around 11.2 million bales," Lange said.

He added that spending for apparel and home furnishings continue to increase in the U.S. "Given that we are not getting much in the way of price inflation, real spending is rising and ought to pull up consumption," he said.
CBOT soybean futures showed weakness from the outset, but rose off the lows on the close.
